title: Prompt-based language model scores multimorbidity to predict mortality across cohorts
summary: A prompt-based large language model multimorbidity score (LLM-MMS), built from health narratives without fine-tuning, was evaluated in 770,439 adults across nine cohorts. In eight external cohorts C-indices were 0.67 to 0.86 and absolute C-index gains over recalibrated conventional comorbidity indices were 0.12 to 0.21. The score is predictive rather than causal, and proteomic analyses were used only to support plausibility.
ai_technology: Prompt-based large language model generating a multimorbidity score from health narratives, no fine-tuning
organization: Department of Thoracic Surgery and Oncology, The First Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University, Guangzhou, China; Yuebei People's Hospital Affiliated to Shantou University Medical College, Shaoguan, China

evidence.unknown: Accuracy of the model-generated scores on individual records and prospective clinical utility; full text not reviewed.
